Public API

Types

LagrangianStochasticConvection.MeanVariable — Type
MeanVariable(name::String, nparticles::Int64, neval::Int64, func::Function)
MeanVariable(name::String, func::Function, kwparams::NamedTuple)

Construct a mean flow quantity from a given recipe func, to be estimated by the kernel-means algorithm

The mean variable $\overline{Q}$ is defined by the particle property $Q^\ast$ in the kernel-means formalism (see Kernel-mean algorithm). The attribute func gives the recipe to build this particle property: it must be a function which takes a Particle as argument, and returns a Float.

The name of the mean variable serves as unique identifier, and should hint at the physical nature of the mean (for example "velocity").

nparticles (resp. neval) is the number of particle locations (resp. fixed regular grid locations) at which the mean flow variable is expected to be estimated. A NamedTuple can be passed instead, provided in contains a field "nparticles", a field "neval_x" and a field "neval_y" (the latter two should correspond to the number of rows and columns in the grid, the product of which corresponds to neval).

The values and derivatives of the mean variable estimated at the particle locations are stored as Vectors of Float in MeanVariable.mean_part, MeanVariable.gradx_part, MeanVariable.grady_part, MeanVariable.hessxx_part, MeanVariable.hessxy_part and MeanVariable.hessyy_part. Those estimated on the fixed regular grid are stored in MeanVariable.mean_eval, MeanVariable.gradx_eval, MeanVariable.grady_eval, MeanVariable.hessxx_eval, MeanVariable.hessxy_eval and MeanVariable.hessyy_eval.

LagrangianStochasticConvection.Particle — Type
Particle(id::Int64, mass::Float64)
Particle(id::Int64, mass::Float64, x::Float64, y::Float64, ux::Float64, uy::Float64, uz::Float64, e::Float64, omega::Float64)

Construct a notional particle identified by an integer id and a (constant) mass. Its initial position, velocity, energy and turbulent frequency can also be passed to the constructor (if not provided, default to 0.0).

The physical properties of the particle are its 2D coordinates Particle.x and Particle.y, its 3D velocity Particle.ux, Particle.uy and Particle.uz, its specific internal energy Particle.e, its turbulent frequency Particle.omega and the lumped volume of fluid it represents Particle.volume.

In addition, the properties of the mean flow at the particle positions are stored in a dictionnary Particle.means, where the keys are in the form "XXX_YYY", where "XXX" is the name of the MeanVariable, and "YYY" is either "mean", "gradx", "grady" or "laplacian".

LagrangianStochasticConvection.MeanComputer — Type
MeanComputer(nmodes::Int64, nparticles::Int64, neval_x::Int64, neval_y::Int64,
			 ncellx::Int64, ncells_y::Int64, Lx::Float64, Ly::Float64, kernel_func::Function)
MeanComputer(kernel_func::Function, kwparams::NamedTuple)

Construct a wrapper with all necessary information to feed the kernel-means algorithm.

The kernel function kernel_func used in the algorithm should take two Floats as argument (distance where the function must be estimated, and size of compact support), and return a Float. It will be expanded onto nmodes Fourier components. Means will be estimated at nparticles particle locations, or alternatively at the nodes of a fixed, regular 2D grid with neval_x rows and neval_y columns. The full domain in which the particles are expected to live has dimensions (Lx, Ly). The kernel-means algorithm requires the domain be paved by a regular 2D grid of rectangular cells. The size of the grid is (ncells_x, ncells_y).

Instead of being passed one by one to the constructor, the parameters can be embedded in a single named tuple kwparams, provided it has all the required field "nmodes", "nparticles", "neval_x", "neval_y", "ncells_x", "ncells_y", "Lx" and "Ly".

In addition, the size of the compact support of the kernel function is stored as (MeanComputer.hx, MeanComputer.hy). By construction, they give the dimensions of the $\mathcal{R}$ cells, and they equal Lx/ncells_x and Ly/ncells_y. The dimensions of the $\mathcal{S}$ cells are also stored in (MeanComputer.lx, MeanComputer.ly), and equal $3 h_x$ and $3 h_y$ by default.

The 2D coordinates of all the Particles representing the flow are meant to be stored as a Positions in MeanComputer.part_pos, and likewise the nodes of the fixed, regular 2D grid is stored in MeanComputer.eval_pos.

The Fourier coefficients of the kernel function are meant to be stored in MeanComputer.ap and MeanComputer.aq as vectors of size nmodes (respectively for the horizontal and vertical parts), and the full list of SmallCells and BigCells used to pave the domain should be stored in MeanComputer.smallcells and MeanComputer.bigcells

Fluid particles

LagrangianStochasticConvection.write_means_to_particles! — Function
write_means_to_particles!(particles::Vector{Particle}, variables::MeanVariable...)

Transfer the value of each MeanVariable (and their spatial derivatives) to each Particle location were it was estimated.

For each variable, the function first reads variable.mean_part, variable.gradx_part, variable.grady_part and variable.hessxx_part + variable.hessyy_part. It then creates or updates particle.means["XXX_mean"], particle.means["XXX_gradx"], particle.means["XXX_grady"] and particle.means["XXX_laplacian"] for each particle in particles, with "XXX" being the name of the variable.

LagrangianStochasticConvection.advance_flow! — Function
number_bad_particles = advance_flow!(particles::Vector{Particle}, drift_velocity_x::Function, drift_velocity_y::Function,
                                     drift_velocity_z::Function, drift_energy::Function, drift_frequency::Function,
                                     diffusion_velocity_x::Function, diffusion_velocity_y::Function,
                                     diffusion_velocity_z::Function, diffusion_energy::Function, diffusion_frequency::Function,
                                     extra_diffusion_frequency::Function, kwparams::NamedTuple)

Evolves each Particle in particles by one time step, according to a given stochastic model, using a Predictor/Corrector scheme. Also applies boundary conditions, checks Courant accuracy condition, and compute the new lumped volume of every particle.

The functions drift_velocity_x, drift_velocity_y, drift_velocity_z, drift_energy and drift_frequency represent the drift coefficients in the Lagrangian stochastic model. They must all take a Particle and a NamedTuple as argument, and return a Float. The named tuple kwparams will be passed to each of them, and must contain all constant parameters required for each of the coefficients of the stochastic model.

Likewise, diffusion_velocity_x, diffusion_velocity_y, diffusion_velocity_z, diffusion_energy and diffusion_frequency represent the diffusion coefficients in the Lagrangian stochastic model.

The function extra_diffusion_frequency represent the derivative of the square of diffusion_frequency with respect to $\omega^\ast$.

In addition to the constant parameters of the stochastic model, kwparams must contain all the fields necessary for the methods apply_boundary_conditions! and check_particle_sanity!.

Return an integer number_bad_particles representing the number of particles that were deemed invalid after the time step (see check_particle_sanity! for more info).

LagrangianStochasticConvection.standard_means! — Function
standard_means!(mean_computer::MeanComputer, evaluating_on_particle_positions::Bool, variables::MeanVariable...)

Compute mean flow variables and their spatial derivatives through a kernel-means formalism. By default, the means are estimated at every particle location, based on mean_computer.part_pos. If is_on_grid == true, they are estimated at every node of a regular rectangular grid instead, based on mean_computer.eval_pos. The means are stored in variable.XXX_part (if is_on_grid == false) or variable.XXX_eval (if is_on_grid == true) for every variable in variables, where XXX refers to "mean", "gradx", "grady", "hessxx", "hessxy" and "hessyy" for the value of the mean variable, its gradient, and its hessian matrix.

Arguments:

  • mean_computer is the MeanComputer wrapping all relevant information for the kernel-means algorithm
  • variables is the set of MeanVariables updated by the method

Corrective scheme

LagrangianStochasticConvection.common_mean_variables — Function
common_mean_variables(npart::Int64, neval::Int64)
common_mean_variables(kwparams::NamedTuple)

Construct instances of MeanVariable for $Q^\ast = \mathcal{V}^\ast$, $\mathcal{V}^\ast x^\ast$, $\mathcal{V}^\ast y^\ast$, $\mathcal{V}^\ast x^{\ast ~ 2}$, $\mathcal{V}^\ast x^\ast y^\ast$ and $\mathcal{V}^\ast y^{\ast ~ 2}$, where $\mathcal{V}^\ast$ is the lumped volume of the particle, and $x^\ast$ and $y^\ast$ its 2D coordinates.

If passed a Named Tuple, it must have a nparticles field for the number of particles, and fields neval_x and neval_y for the number of rows and columns in the 2D grid.

Arguments:

  • npart is the number of particles location where the means of these variables are to be estimated
  • neval is the number of nodes in the regular rectangular grid where the means of these variables are to be estimated

Returns:

  • the MeanVariables corresponding to all 6 quantities
source
LagrangianStochasticConvection.corrective_SPH! — Function
corrective_SPH!(mean_computer::MeanComputer, W::MeanVariable, X::MeanVariable, Y::MeanVariable, XX::MeanVariable,
                XY::MeanVariable, YY::MeanVariable, variables::MeanVariable...; is_on_grid::Bool=false)

Apply the corrective kernel estimation scheme to each MeanVariable in variables. The means W, X, Y, XX, XY and YY must be computed in advance (see Correcting the kernel-mean estimate for explanation). The mean variables are modified in place.

By default, the means estimated at the particle locations are corrected, based on mean_computer.part_pos. If is_on_grid == true, the means estimated at the nodes of the regular rectangular grid are corrected instead, based on mean_computer.eval_pos.

LagrangianStochasticConvection.divide_by_density! — Function
divide_by_density!(density::MeanVariable, variables::MeanVariable...; is_on_grid::Bool=false)

Same as divide_by_density_one_variable!, but for several MeanVariables at once. Any number of arguments can be passed to this method, and starting from the second one, they will be treated as mean variables to be divided by density.

Simulation initialisation

LagrangianStochasticConvection.read_config_file — Function
read_config_file(filename::String)

Read all constant parameters necessary to run a simulation from a configuration file. The parameters are written to a single NamedTuple returned by this function.

If the output directory specified in the configuration file does not exist, it is created. The configuration file is also copied under the name "config.toml" in the output directory.

source
LagrangianStochasticConvection.initialise_all_particles — Function
initialise_all_particles(kwparams::NamedTuple)

Construct all Particles that will be used in a simulation, based on simulation parameters contained within the named tuple kwparams. The particles are initialised from scratch, at random.

source
LagrangianStochasticConvection.read_all_particles_from_file — Function
read_all_particles_from_file!(kwparams::NamedTuple)

Construct all Particles that will be used in a simulation, based on simulation parameters contained within the named tuple kwparams. The particles are read from a text file "initial_directory/raw_output/final_state.dat", where initial_directory must be a field of kwparams.

The number of particles specified by kwparams, under the field nparticles, must correspond to the number of particles in the input file.

Output

LagrangianStochasticConvection.display_simu_params — Function
display_simu_params(kwparams::NamedTuple)

Print information about the simulation being run, based on the contents of kwparams. The named tuple must contain the following fields:

  • "Ly" for the horizontal size of the domain
  • "ncells_x" and "ncells_y" for the number of $\mathcal{R}$cells in the kernel-mean formalism
  • "ntime" and "dt" for the number and duration of time steps
  • "nparticles" for the number of particles
  • "npoly", "gamma1", "gravity" and "kappa" for the polytropic index, adiabatic exponent, gravitational acceleration and radiative diffusivity
  • "ebot" and "etop" for the imposed bottom energy and top energy
  • "initial_directory" and "save_directory" for the directory where the initial state of the particles is read, and the directory where the output of the present simulation will be saved
source
LagrangianStochasticConvection.save_mean_output — Function
save_mean_output(id::Int64, save_dir::String, type::String, mean_computer::MeanComputer, variables::MeanVariable...)

Write estimates of the means of each variable in variables at each node of a predetermined regular 2D grid contained in mean_computer to a text file. The text file is saved under XXX/raw_output/ZZZ_YYYYYY.dat, where XXX = save_dir, and YYYYYY = id, padded with zeros to form a 6-digit number, and ZZZ == type is the type of means being saved (must be either "mean", "gradx", "grady", or "laplacian").

source
LagrangianStochasticConvection.save_particle_output — Function
save_particle_output(id::Int64, save_dir::String, particles::Vector{Particle})

Write the properties of all particles in particles to a text file. The text file is saved under XXX/raw_output/particles_YYYYYY.dat, where XXX = save_dir, and YYYYYY = id, padded with zeros to form a 6-digit number. If id < 0, the text file is saved under save_dir/final_state.dat instead.
